title: Brown County Council members question mid-year change to 40-hour week policy
text:
← Back to the wire

Brown County Council members question mid-year change to 40-hour week policy
A council member said the current salary ordinance was based on a 40-hour week with a paid lunch, and asked whether pay should instead be recalculated on a 37.5-hour week with an unpaid lunch for the rest of the year.
At the Brown County Council work session held Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026, a council member raised concerns about a proposed change to employee work hours and lunch policy that would take effect before the end of the year.
THE CONCERN A council member said the existing salary ordinance was approved based on a policy with a 40-hour work week including a paid lunch hour, and that this was publicly posted and recorded. The council member argued that "for the remainder of the year, our salary should be divided by 37 and a half hours and we take a half hour unpaid lunch," adding that salaries should not otherwise change from what was advertised.
HISTORICAL CONTEXT The council member recalled that the county previously operated on a 35-hour work week with an unpaid lunch under a past auditor, after the state board of accounts intervened over how employees recorded lunch hours on time sheets. "We didn't have a human resource department," the council member said, describing confusion at the time over exempt status and overtime.
IMPACT ON OFFICES A council member objected to proposed hours that would keep offices open from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. but require staff to arrive at 7:30 a.m. or stay until 4:30 p.m. to receive a 40-hour paycheck. "It makes no sense for my employees to come in at 7:30 when they are not helping the taxpayers because that's what we're here for," the council member said, adding that the office does not close for lunch and that coordination between departments, including the treasurer's, auditor's, assessor's and recorder's offices, would be difficult if offices were not all staffed at the same times.
No vote was taken on the matter during the discussion.
